{{nihongo|'''Shiritaogi Shrine'''|志理太乎宜神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

During the Edo period it was called '''Kinomiya Shrine''' (きのみやじんじゃ), and this name is still used today as an alternative name, appearing on items such as the plaque on the torii gate<ref name="kotobank">[https://kotobank.jp/word/白田村-3062457 What is Shirada Village] - Kotobank</ref><ref name="engi-chosa">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140133-02.html Shiritaogi Shrine] - Survey of Engishiki Shrines</ref>.

=== Overview ===
The shrine is located immediately west of {{ill|Katase-Shirata Station|Q6375267|qid=Q6375267}}, along {{ill|Japan National Route 135|Q6156779|qid=Q6156779}}.

Together with {{ill|Shiitori Shrine|Q134930749|qid=Q134930749}} on {{ill|Miyake-jima|Q1075076|qid=Q1075076}}, it is regarded as a candidate shrine (ronsha) of '''Shirita(ogi) Shrine''' (しりた(お)き[ぎ]じんじゃ), a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} that enshrines Shirita(ogi)-no-Mikoto, one of the princes of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mishima Daimyōjin}} ({{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}}). Meanwhile, {{ill|Katasuge Shrine|Q134892414|qid=Q134892414|lt=Katasuge Shrine}} in the neighboring Katase district to the north—thought to have been founded around the same time—also serves as a candidate Shikinaisha enshrining another prince of Mishima Daimyōjin (Kotoshironushi-no-Kami) of Miyakejima, competing with {{ill|Katasuge Shrine|Q134930291|qid=Q134930291}} on Miyakejima itself. Because of this branch-shrine–like relationship, it is possible that these shrines were originally established as refugee branch shrines or distant worship sites relocated from Miyakejima to avoid volcanic eruptions<ref name="engi-chosa"/><ref name="engi-chosa2">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140116-04.html Katasuge Shrine] - Survey of Engishiki Shrines</ref><ref name="choshi"/>.

Although the date of foundation is unknown, a record of reconstruction in the 2nd year of {{ill|Kōei|Q980266|qid=Q980266}} ({{ill|1343|Q6072|qid=Q6072}}) appears in the *Nantō Fudoki*<ref name="choshi">[https://www.town.higashiizu.shizuoka.jp/bg/life/upload/kyo_higashiizutyousi_30mini_6.pdf *History of Higashiizu Town*, Chapter 6, p. 360] - Higashiizu Town</ref>. In addition, ridgepole inscriptions from the 2nd year of {{ill|Jōwa (Muromachi period)|Q1146143|qid=Q1146143}} ({{ill|1346|Q6080|qid=Q6080}}) record the name '''Shirada Ki(hama) Shrine''' (しらだき(はま)じんじゃ) (*Zōtei Tōshū Shikō*)<ref name="kotobank"/>.

As indicated by its former shrine name and the enshrined deity {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}}, during the Edo period it also strongly exhibited the character of a Kinomiya Shrine associated with {{ill|Kinomiya Faith|Q11296898|qid=Q11296898}}. Even today, like {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawazu Kinomiya Shrine}} ({{ill|Sugihokowake no Mikoto Shrine|Q11522170|qid=Q11522170}}) in {{ill|Kawazu, Shizuoka|Q1203861|qid=Q1203861}}, it retains the cultural tradition known as “{{ill|bird abstinence and sake abstinence|Q11553983|qid=Q11553983|lt=bird abstinence and sake abstinence}}”<ref name="engi-chosa"/><ref name="yuisho">On-site shrine history plaque</ref><ref name="ss">[https://www.at-s.com/facilities/article/view/temple/137787.html Kinomiya Shrine (Higashiizu Town)] - Shizuoka Shimbun</ref>.
